brands.evidence: Foreign purchases have no transaction fee, but watch for charges on withdrawals.
Starling is the best all-round pick for fee-free spending abroad.
Both are fine for spending, but their free ATM allowances are tighter.
Chase allows fee-free cash withdrawals overseas, up to set limits.

client_claims.text: Starling's debit card is fee-free for all purchases and cash withdrawals, unlike rival Monzo.
client_claims.note: Implies Monzo is not fee-free for cash; F7 shows allowances then a 3% fee, so it is vague rather than contradicted.

client_claims.text: Monzo: Foreign purchases have no transaction fee.
Monzo cash withdrawals are fee-free in the EEA, and up to £200 a month elsewhere, if Monzo is your main account.
client_claims.note: Fact says £200 every 30 days outside the EEA on the free plan, with unlimited EEA only if main bank; the £400 EEA allowance applies otherwise. The 'if main account' condition and 'a month' do not match.

client_claims.text: Watch for charges on Monzo withdrawals.
client_claims.note: A 3% fee applies after the allowance.
